synthesis: A Scout check-in is meant to assert 'this kit was at this location'. ScoutCheckInMatchQuery currently GROUP BYs address_id, so it actually asserts 'this kit was near this address record' — N distinct address rows sharing one exact coordinate each produce their own persisted scout_check_ins row for a single physical visit. Measured on the live book, ~48% of open-order address rows share a geo with at least one other row, so this fan-out is systemic, not an edge case. The fix regroups on the address's exact geo and uses ROW_NUMBER() to elect one canonical address per (geo, hour_bucket) — Direct-wins, then lowest address_id — whose address_id/hotlist_id/is_staged persist. The dashboard tile (ScoutCheckInRollupQuery) must move in lockstep on the geo-dedup but must NOT adopt Direct-wins: it deliberately counts a Direct+Staging shared location once in each bucket, so its dedup runs independently per is_staged bucket. No migration, no backfill, no schedule re-enable.

scope.summary: Restructure the CTE chain in both ClickHouse query classes to dedup on exact address geo instead of address_id, electing one canonical address per (geo, hour_bucket) via ROW_NUMBER(). Layer the new geo-level rank ON TOP of today's existing per-address collapse rather than replacing it. Update both class docblocks. No PHP-side logic, schema, schedule or config changes.

proposed_changes.change: Add `a.addr_lng` / `a.addr_lat` to the `matches` CTE projection (it does not carry them today). Insert a new `address_hour` CTE that is EXACTLY today's final aggregate — unchanged `argMin(hotlist_id, (toUInt8(is_staged), hotlist_id))`, `min(is_staged)`, single-tuple `argMin((lng,lat), timestamp_utc)`, `min(timestamp_utc)` — but GROUP BY (address_id, addr_lng, addr_lat, hour_bucket). Then a `ranked` CTE adding ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY addr_lng, addr_lat, hour_bucket ORDER BY toUInt8(is_staged) ASC, address_id ASC) AS rn. Final SELECT reads `FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1`, projecting the same out_* column names/shape as today.
proposed_changes.reason: Required changes #1/#2/#3. The two-level nesting is REQUIRED, not stylistic: today's argMin resolves one address_id sitting on MULTIPLE hotlists (Direct-wins, then lowest hotlist_id). A single-pass rank ordered only by (is_staged, address_id) ties on BOTH keys for those rows and picks arbitrarily, regressing a documented semantic and making the parity test flaky. Layering keeps the change a strict superset of current behavior.
proposed_changes.agreement: 4/4 passes plus the driver's own source read independently reached the layered design

proposed_changes.change: Update the class docblock: replace the '(address, hour-bucket)' / 'Positions are grouped by (address_id, toStartOfHour(timestamp_utc))' grain language with the (address geo, hour-bucket) grain and the two-level priority rule (intra-address hotlist tie-break unchanged; new inter-address Direct-wins-then-lowest-address_id geo election). proposed_changes.reason: Required change #5. Keep it tight — this repo's owner prefers sparse docblocks.

proposed_changes.change: Add `a.addr_lng` / `a.addr_lat` to the `matches` CTE (today it selects DISTINCT address_id, is_staged, hour_bucket). Add a `ranked` CTE: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY is_staged, addr_lng, addr_lat, hour_bucket ORDER BY address_id ASC) AS rn. Final SELECT becomes countIf(is_staged = false AND rn = 1) / countIf(is_staged = true AND rn = 1) FROM ranked. Leave the `addresses` CTE untouched — its DISTINCT serves book-row dedup, a different concern.
proposed_changes.reason: Required change #4. Putting is_staged IN the partition key is what preserves the both-buckets semantic: each partition holds only one is_staged value, so Direct and Staging each elect their own winner and a shared location still counts once in EACH bucket. No Direct-wins ordering here — that would silently delete staging counts.
proposed_changes.driver_decision: Passes split on shape: the fast pass proposed a one-line `SELECT DISTINCT addr_lng, addr_lat, is_staged, hour_bucket` swap; candidates 1/2/3 proposed the ROW_NUMBER mirror. All FOUR are arithmetically identical for a COUNT output (DISTINCT over the 4-tuple == rn=1 over the same partition). Driver picks ROW_NUMBER for two grounded reasons: (a) the ticket's own wording asks for 'the geo-dedup + address_id ASC pick within each bucket', and DISTINCT performs no pick; (b) ScoutCheckInMatchQueryParityTest exists precisely to bind these two classes' architecture, so structural symmetry is the maintained invariant. Recorded as a decision, not a silent pick.

proposed_changes.change: Update the class docblock grain description to the geo grain + per-bucket-independent dedup, keeping the existing note that a shared Direct+Staging address counts in both buckets.

questions.q: The ticket says it_records_multiple_in_radius_addresses_in_one_cycle 'REVERSES' and must become a distinct-geo test. Is that correct?
questions.answer: No — the ticket's premise is factually wrong about this fixture. Its three spots are (-97.70,30.30) / (-97.80,30.40) / (-97.90,30.50), measured ~14.7-29.4 km apart pairwise — orders of magnitude beyond both the 160.934m radius and the ~330m bbox pad. The test ALREADY exercises AC3 and its assertion of 3 rows must NOT change. Only the NAME is misleading. The scenario the ticket actually describes (co-located, distinct address_ids at one geo) has no coverage under any existing test name and must be added fresh. Following the ticket literally here would have damaged a correct test.
questions.agreement: independently measured by all three blind candidates

questions.q: Must the existing per-address argMin(hotlist_id, ...) tie-break be retained, or does the ticket's one-line ROW_NUMBER replace it outright?
questions.answer: It MUST be retained as a first stage. It resolves one address_id sitting on multiple hotlists (Direct-wins, then lowest hotlist_id). Under a single-pass rank ordered only by (toUInt8(is_staged), address_id), two such rows tie on BOTH sort keys and ClickHouse elects arbitrarily — regressing a documented semantic and destabilising test_duplicate_book_rows_for_one_address_produce_one_match. The ticket's phrase 'address_id ASC replaces the current hotlist_id tie-break as the address-level decider' means it decides among DIFFERENT addresses at one geo; it does not remove the within-address decider.
questions.agreement: 4/4 passes plus the driver's own read

questions.q: Does ClickHouse support ROW_NUMBER() in this CTE-then-filter shape, and does this repo already do it?
questions.answer: Yes on both. ROW_NUMBER() has been supported since ClickHouse ~21.3 (pinned version here is 26.2), and window functions are already used in-repo: RecoveryLeaderQuery.php:24 (sum(...) OVER (PARTITION BY recovery_id)), plus row_number() OVER in Hit.php:416-417 and LeaderboardTableWidget.php:42. Both target classes are ClickHouse-only and exercised solely under RequiresClickhouse, so no pgsql-bridge dialect branch is needed.

questions.q: EXACT-geo dedup at real production scale: the live book holds a single exact coordinate carrying 20,396 open-order address rows (org 165, ~north Texas) and a second carrying 6,482 rows at a point in American Samoa; ~48% of all 4.53M book rows share a geo with at least one other row. The ticket justifies exact-Point equality as 'deliberately conservative', on the premise that identical coordinates mean genuine co-location (duplicated geocode, apartment complex, multi-unit lot). Clusters of 20k+ and an implausible-territory point look like geocoder-fallback centroids or sentinels, not real co-location. Is collapsing such a cluster to ONE check-in per kit-hour the intended behavior, or should the matcher exclude/deprioritise mass-shared coordinates?
questions.answer: INVESTIGATED (2026-08-24) — see docs/investigations/DEV-2414/cluster-investigation.md. VERDICT: the mega-clusters are geocoder-fallback / sentinel artifacts, not real shared addresses. Decisive evidence is the multi-org signature: C1 (-96.808028, 33.083789) carries 20,402 addresses across 17,722 hotlists and 32 DISTINCT ORGS; C2 is Pago Pago, American Samoa (-170.701384, -14.273749) with 6,482 addresses across 49 orgs. No real building hosts open repo orders for 32-49 unrelated repo companies, and no company has 6,482 open orders in American Samoa. DESIGN CONSEQUENCE: at a fallback centroid there is NO true location signal to preserve, so exact-Point dedup cannot 'hide' genuine orders there. Today a kit within 160.934m of C1 records 20,402 false check-ins in one kit-hour; after the change it records 1. The dedup is STRICTLY PROTECTIVE at exactly the clusters that raised the concern -> ship exact-Point as the ticket specifies, no mass-shared-coordinate guard in the matcher. EXPOSURE IS LATENT, NOT ACTIVE: the largest baseline run recorded 138 across 44 kits, so no kit came within 160.934m of these clusters during the 2h window; none of the 2.07/kit figure is attributable to them. FOLLOW-UP ELSEWHERE: excluding fallback coordinates belongs upstream in chlocal's scout_open_addresses_mv (migration 111), alongside the status=Open / length(plate)>3 / EWKT filters -- separate ticket.
questions.materiality: MATERIAL — data semantics. Cannot be auto-answered (non-negotiable 1).
questions.driver_framing: The risk runs BOTH ways and that sharpens rather than blocks the change. Under TODAY's code a kit passing within 160.934m of that point with those orders open fans out to ~20,396 rows in a single insertOrIgnore for one kit-hour — a latent incident the current grain already carries. The new dedup caps it at 1, so this change is strictly protective on volume. The open question is only the semantic one: whether collapsing to one row unacceptably HIDES genuinely distinct open orders. Note also that address geocoding and the book rebuild are chlocal-owned, so an exclusion rule would likely belong upstream, not here.

resource_envelope.allocation_sketch: No new PHP-side allocation. The recorder's per-org/per-kit loop is untouched and stays O(matches) per DEV-2342/PG-026; this ticket adds no accumulator, chunk, or PHP-side collection. The new ROW_NUMBER runs ENTIRELY server-side in ClickHouse over the set already narrowed by the per-kit ~330m bbox pad and the 160.934m geoDistance join — not the 4.53M-row fleet book, not the 849k-row largest-org slice. Worst-case new partition size is bounded by the largest exact-geo cluster that can fall inside one kit's bbox: measured at 20,396 rows fleet-wide, which ClickHouse ranks trivially.
